findings.title: Global group view permission grants group management
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates both `view` and `manage` on the all-groups resource. Consequently, a principal granted only the `view` scope for Groups passes `requireManage()` and can create top-level groups, as well as perform management operations that use the global check. The global management check must require only the `manage` scope; `view` should only be accepted by view/list checks.

findings.title: Group-member user searches are filtered using authorization resource IDs
findings.body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `groupResource.getId()`, which is the authorization Resource entity ID. The user search/count overloads consume this set as realm `GroupModel` IDs (the V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name). Authorization resources are created with the group ID as their name, but have a distinct generated resource ID, so admins with `view-members` or `manage-members` on an individual group will not receive that group's users in filtered user searches/counts. Add `groupResource.getName()` (the group model ID) instead.

findings.title: Master-admin role no longer grants per-user view/manage access in V2
findings.body: This removes `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the direct per-user `canView` and `canManage` checks. A master-realm administrator with the `admin` role managing another realm is not in the target realm (`isAdminSameRealm()` is false), so after this change authorization-resource fallback cannot restore access. Such administrators will receive forbidden responses for direct user operations that previously succeeded. Preserve the `ADMIN` bypass (and apply the corresponding super-admin semantics consistently to the new group evaluator).
